discovery: Optical metamaterials and metasurfaces: designing the electromagnetic response of matter through subwavelength structure
motivation: Pendry showed theoretically that artificial subwavelength structures can give effective permittivity and permeability not found in nature, predicting negative refraction, the perfect lens and transformation optics. Smith realized the first negative-index metamaterial and, with Pendry, the first electromagnetic cloak, proving that light paths can be designed at will. Capasso turned these ideas into flat optics: metasurfaces that impose abrupt phase shifts, formulating generalized laws of reflection and refraction and demonstrating ultrathin metalenses now entering industrial production. Together they created a new paradigm in which the optical properties of matter are engineered through geometry rather than chemistry. The concept has transformed nanophotonics, imaging, sensing, optical computing, wireless communication and photovoltaic light management, and is used by thousands of laboratories worldwide. It is an outstanding example of fundamental physics that has reached from basic electromagnetism to widely deployed technology.
